## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded by [source-6@L56-L72|claim=ordinary-document]. It establishes only the conjectural status of the stronger general statement.
- claim-2: Correct conditional on the accepted formulas \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\) and the rectangle bounds. From \(a=1,b=2\), both complementary dimensions are positive, at least one equals \(1\), and \(i,j\ge2\) with at least one equal to \(2\).
- claim-3: The Pieri calculations are correct. The box bounds ensure \(x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2,z\) exist; only \(u\) can leave the box. The three displayed products have exactly the stated terms, and subtraction gives \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\). This is an independently checkable local argument, not evidence for elimination in higher degrees.
- claim-4: Correct as a change-of-family statement, even if the classes have relations or torsion. “Basis of its span” should be interpreted as integral linear independence together with generation of that span; neither family has yet been shown to be a basis of \(Q\).
- claim-5: Unproved. The displayed Pieri identities neither eliminate every complementary column nor exclude residual relations or torsion. “Unit-pivot elimination” must be defined as unimodular row operations on the accepted integral relation lattice; otherwise the asserted equivalence with \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^3\) is not automatic. A uniform argument must also handle separately the boundary alternatives \(q-i=1\) and \(r-j=1\).
- The strategy successfully isolates a bounded weaker target, but does not establish the uniform lemma. It therefore reaches the requested research-attempt level only with the conjectural status and unresolved integral issues retained explicitly.

## Required revisions
- Add the omitted low-degree relation
  \[
  h_1y_1=z+y_2+w,\qquad w=s_{(i^j,1,1)},
  \]
  with \(w=0\) when \(r-j=1\). Since \(a=1\), at least one of \(u,w\) is outside the box. The resulting degree-\(ij+2\) block can be audited by unit pivots and may already prove that its quotient is freely generated by \(\bar x_2\).
- Likewise record that the degree-\(ij\) and degree-\(ij+1\) blocks are respectively \(\mathbb Z\bar x_0\) and \(\mathbb Z\bar x_1\). This would separate low-degree independence from the still-unresolved global elimination problem.
- State a precise uniform elimination order, prove termination for every box, and verify that the generated row lattice is saturated. Without saturation, rational independence does not exclude integral torsion.
- Keep \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^3\), global torsion-freeness, and minimality of either family explicitly unresolved until that argument is supplied.
